findings.title: `cf config unset --project` cannot clear the stale shared-file copy and deletes the personal value instead
Migration story covers only the developer who runs `migrate-personal`
findings.description:
The slice plan requires "a defined migration/compat story for projects that already committed personal keys". The design states "reads must not silently drop that value" (line 138), but only analyses a single checkout.

The shared file is committed. Once one developer runs `migrate-personal` and commits the shared-file deletion, every teammate who pulls has the key in neither file. Their `git.integration_branch` silently falls through to user/default, which changes their fork and merge target with no warning, because the check rule only fires while the key is still in the shared file.

State the intended team behaviour: either accept this and print it in the command output, or have the command tell the user that teammates must set their own value before the change is pulled.

findings.title: Existing projects get an un-ignored `.context-forge.local.toml`
findings.description:
The `.gitignore` line is added only by `cf init`, and the success criterion covers only "a fresh project" (line 216). Existing projects are the ones the migration targets. There, `cf config set git.integration_branch … --project` or `migrate-personal` creates the personal file with no ignore entry, so the next `git add .` commits it. That reproduces the leak the plan entry says must never happen.

Either have the new `ConsistencyChecker` rule also warn when the personal file exists but is not ignored, or apply the same one-line ensure when the personal file is first written. Either reuses logic already in the slice.

Separately, the "substring" check (line 159) would treat `#.context-forge.local.toml` or `!.context-forge.local.toml` as already covered. Specify an exact trimmed-line match.

findings.title: `migrate-personal` carries more mechanism than one personal key needs
findings.description:
Exactly one key is classified personal (line 111), yet the command specifies a three-way collision rule, per-key independent processing, continue-past-failure and a `failed: <error>` summary line.

- **Cut:** continue-past-failure and per-key failure reporting. Fail fast on the first error; the write-then-delete ordering already makes a re-run safe, and fail-fast matches the project's "fail explicitly" principle.
- **Cut:** the `skipped (personal value already set)` branch, if the FAIL above is fixed by deleting the stale shared copy.
- **Add:** tests for whatever collision and failure behaviour remains. The Technical Requirements (line 222) list only "happy path + no-op path" for the command.

findings.title: `list()` behaviour under the two-file split is not specified
findings.description: Data Flow defines `get`, `set` and `delete`; `list()` appears only in the component table ("precedence order updated in get()/list()"). Add one line confirming `list()` applies the same per-key fallback and `source` values, so a personal key in the shared file reports `project` in both.

findings.title: Dependency declaration differs from the slice plan
findings.description: The frontmatter lists `dependencies: [914]` and the body cites the 916 prerequisite fix; the plan entry for 915 says "Dependencies: none". 914 and 916 are both complete, so this is harmless, but the plan entry should be updated to match.
